**Required Role:** Viewer or higher

query.description: A comma separated list of collection guids, for to filter the collection items from
A comma separated list of data source types to filter for those types of data sources that these jobs  belong to. Supported types: ['airflow', 'fivetran', 'openlineage']
A comma separated list of data source guids to filter for items within those data sources.
A boolean to fetch the jobs where target table event type has the ddl statement. Defaults to False.

A boolean to show hidden objects when true and hide hidden objects when false. Defaults to False.

Specify the ordering for the results. 

 A comma separated list for ordering by multiple fields and a preceding `-` indicates reverse order. 

Note: Order is case-sensitive.
A page number within the paginated result set.
Number of results to return per page.
Search for an asset using a collection name
Search for an asset using its description
Search for an asset using its name
A comma separated list of table guids to filter for the jobs affecting the tables

description.content:
Gets a list of related dashboards given a job_guid

**Required Role:** Viewer or higher

query.description: A search term.
A flag allowing to include hidden dashboards in the response.

Specify the ordering for the results. 

 A comma separated list for ordering by multiple fields and a preceding `-` indicates reverse order. 

Note: Order is case-sensitive.
A page number within the paginated result set.
Number of results to return per page.
When `relevant_lineage` is `true`, we only use edges between columns to traverse the graph. Requires relevant lineage to be enabled in the organization; the flag is ignored otherwise.
A search term.
A search term.
A search term.

Filter objects by updated_on. May specify __gt, __gte, __lt or __lte.

 API call to: 

 ENDPOINT/updated_on__gt=2021-08-04T15:12:40&updated_on__lt=2021-08-23 

 will result with objects updated_on after  August 4th 2021 at 15:12:40, but before August 23rd 2021. 

. If you want to include lower or upper bound of the range use __gte or __lte respectively.
